decision_reason: Neither ONT nor Illumina RNA contains the somatic deletion junction. Both instead support canonical DLG5 RNA from an intact allele, so translation of the deletion is withheld.
dna_only: The deletion removes five ENST00000372391 coding exons, including the annotated start codon, but genomic loss does not identify an expressed mutant transcript or a replacement translation start.
epitope_message: Not predicted because no deletion-junction transcript, CDS start, or mutant protein was observed.
interpretation: Long reads phase up to four canonical exon junctions on one molecule while short reads provide deeper local junction support. That platform difference strengthens the intact-transcript interpretation but creates no mutant peptide.
limitation: Reference-spliced RNA may arise from the intact allele; absence of a mutant RNA junction does not prove the DNA event is false or transcriptionally silent in every cell.

platform_comparison.conclusion: Long and short RNA both show canonical DLG5 expression from an intact transcript, but neither contains the somatic deletion junction; no mutant CDS or vaccine peptide is established.
platform_comparison.dna_model: The 79,531-bp deletion removes five ENST00000372391 coding exons, including the chr10:77926518-77926520 start codon. The retained lower-coordinate coding region has no annotated start after the deletion.

overview.long: Two T1 and two T2 reads phase four canonical DLG5 junctions
overview.short: Canonical retained-to-deleted exon junction: 130 T1 / 51 T2 fragments
overview.vaccine: No deletion-junction RNA on either platform; no mutant peptide

rows.evidence: No deletion-junction path. Two reads in each sample span four canonical DLG5 exon junctions, linking retained and DNA-deleted regions on an intact RNA molecule.
